alerts.description: Detection: Detects creation of a local user account on macOS via the osquery `users` table scheduled in DIFFERENTIAL mode: osquery emits an 'added' row only for an account that appeared since the previous interval, and the parser derives the account_created vocabulary token for it (the same token the Windows 4720 path emits). This is the macOS half of the V0.6b rogue-account-creation item (T1136); the Windows half is windows_local_account_created. The two rules are keyed apart by the `source` column (osquery:users vs osquery:windows_events) so one event cannot fire both. HONEST BEHAVIOR NOTES (validated live on the reference daemon, 2026-09-14): (1) the first schedule tick after an osquery (re)start stores the baseline SILENTLY -- no rows are emitted and there is NO restart burst; a stable account set emits nothing, so this rule fires only when an account actually appears on the host. (2) logged_in_users is deliberately NOT part of this detection: utmpx rows are session state (auth_success/session_closed tokens) -- a login session is not an account creation. (3) Deleted accounts ('removed' rows) carry no token -- the closed vocabulary has no account_deleted token; the raw rows survive in raw_data. The schedule filters to uid >= 500 (real accounts on macOS; system accounts stay below 500).
